title: Show the least
sub: Film 3 of 8 of Only what you may see, the second series of Data protection and privacy: the nine ways to hide a value, what each lets a reader see, whether it can be undone and by whom, and what still works; why a way that can be undone keeps data personal, why hidden isn't anonymous, and why a small count needs one more hidden beside it.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's look, Night glass: a dark hall of frosted glass panes, light along their edges. Cyan is a person or an agent, green what's allowed, coral what's closed or leaks, violet hidden personal data, gold each column's class. Frost over a value means it's encrypted: all there, unreadable without its key. The story of 1856 is painted by lamplight, at dusk.
